parts.name: Multiple-choice cloze
parts.instr: For questions 1–8, read the text below and decide which answer (A, B, C or D) best fits each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.example: 0 — A considered  B thought  C believed  D regarded → A
parts.title: Who owns street art?
paras: Not long ago, painting on walls was (0) considered vandalism, and artists had to work quickly at night to [[1]] being caught. Today, however, many cities actively [[2]] street artists to brighten up neglected neighbourhoods.

Some of these artists have become [[3]] famous. Their work is photographed by tourists, shared millions of times online and, occasionally, cut out of walls and sold for huge sums. This has [[4]] to an interesting debate: who does a piece of street art actually [[5]] to – the artist, the owner of the wall, or the public?

For many artists, the answer is clear. Street art, they argue, only makes [[6]] in the place where it was created. Once it is removed, it [[7]] much of its meaning. Others are more relaxed, pointing out that nothing painted on a city wall is [[8]] to last forever anyway.

q.expl: avoid + -ing — избежать: avoid being caught. Prevent требует дополнения (prevent sb from), protect — from, refuse — to + инфинитив.
invite sb to do sth — приглашать кого-то что-то сделать. С welcome, admit и agree такой конструкции нет.
internationally famous — известный во всём мире. Greatly, highly, deeply с famous не сочетаются.
lead to sth — привести к чему-то. Resulted нужен с in, brought — с about, caused идёт без предлога.
belong to sb — принадлежать кому-то. Own/possess/have используются наоборот: who owns it?, без to.
Устойчивое make sense — иметь смысл. Make meaning/point/reason так не говорят.
lose its meaning — терять смысл. Miss — скучать или пропустить, drop — уронить, fail — провалить.
be meant to — быть предназначенным для чего-то: nothing is meant to last forever.

parts.name: Open cloze
parts.instr: For questions 9–16, read the text below and think of the word which best fits each gap. Use only one word in each gap. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: In praise of boredom
paras: Most of us do everything we can to avoid feeling bored. As (0) soon as there is a quiet moment, we reach for our phones. But according to some psychologists, boredom is not [[9]] bad as we think.

In one well-known experiment, participants were asked to do a very dull task, such as copying numbers from a list, before [[10]] given a creative challenge. Those who had been bored first came up [[11]] more original ideas than those who had not.

The explanation seems to be that when the brain has nothing interesting to focus [[12]], it starts to wander. This kind of daydreaming allows us to make connections between ideas that we might otherwise never have noticed.

[[13]] course, this does not mean that we should spend all day staring at the wall. However, it might be worth leaving our phones in our pockets now and [[14]]. As one researcher put it, 'Boredom is the brain's way of telling us to do something different. [[15]] we always ignore it, we may be missing [[16]] on our best ideas.'

q.expl: Сравнение not as … as — не такой… как. В отрицании допустимо и not so … as.
После предлога before нужна -ing форма, а по смыслу пассив: before being given — перед тем, как им дали задание.
Фразовый глагол come up with — придумать (идею).
focus on sth — сосредоточиться на чём-то; предлог остаётся в конце придаточного.
Of course — конечно.
now and then (или now and again) — время от времени.
Условие: If we always ignore it, we may be missing…
miss out on sth — упустить возможность.

parts.name: Word formation
parts.instr: For questions 17–24, read the text below. Use the word given in capitals at the end of some of the lines to form a word that fits in the gap in the same line. There is an example at the beginning (0).
parts.title: Working from home
paras: In recent years, (0) millions of people have started working from home, at least part of the time. For many, the [[17]] is the biggest advantage: they can organise their day around their family and avoid long, [[18]] journeys to the office.

However, working from home also has its [[19]]. Some employees struggle with [[20]], especially if they live alone, while others find it hard to switch off and end up answering emails late at night. Many miss the [[21]] chats with colleagues that make office life more enjoyable.

Employers, too, have mixed feelings. While some report that their staff are more [[22]] at home, others worry about the [[23]] of training new employees remotely. It seems [[24]] that the future of work will be a mixture of both.

q.expl: После the нужно существительное: flexibility — гибкость.
Перед journeys нужно прилагательное: stressful — напряжённый. Ловушка: stressed описывает человека, а не поездку.
However показывает контраст с плюсами, значит, нужны минусы: disadvantages (устойчиво: has its advantages and disadvantages).
После struggle with нужно существительное: loneliness — одиночество.
Перед chats нужно прилагательное: friendly — дружеские.
more productive — продуктивнее; после more нужно прилагательное.
После the нужно существительное: difficulty (или difficulties) of training.
It seems likely that… — похоже, вероятно, что…

parts.name: Key word transformation
parts.instr: For questions 25–30, complete the second sentence so that it has a similar meaning to the first sentence, using the word given. Do not change the word given. You must use between two and five words, including the word given.
parts.example: 0 What type of music do you like best? FAVOURITE → What IS YOUR FAVOURITE type of music?

q.first: It's possible that Sarah missed the bus.
q.expl: Предположение о прошлом: might have + V3.

q.first: I've never seen such a beautiful sunset.
q.before: This is the most beautiful sunset
q.expl: Превосходная степень + I have ever + V3: the most beautiful sunset I have ever seen.

q.first: They are building a new hospital in our town.
q.expl: Пассив в Present Continuous: is being built.

q.first: I don't have enough money to buy a new phone.
q.expl: can't afford (to buy) sth — не могу себе позволить.

q.first: He didn't study, so he failed the exam.
q.before: He wouldn't have failed the exam
q.expl: Третий тип условных: wouldn't have failed … if he had studied.

q.first: The last time I spoke to Emma was in March.
q.expl: The last time I did… was… ⇄ I haven't done… since…. Present Perfect с since.

parts.name: Multiple choice
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a young violin maker. For questions 31–36, choose the answer (A, B, C or D) which you think fits best according to the text.
parts.title: Made by hand
parts.subtitle: At nineteen, Ruth Okoye is one of the youngest professional violin makers in the country. She talks to Ben Carter about her unusual career.
paras: Ruth Okoye's workshop smells of wood and varnish. Half-finished instruments hang from the ceiling, and the floor is covered in thin curls of wood. 'My mum says it looks like a hamster's cage,' Ruth laughs. 'She's probably right, but I know exactly where everything is.' She has been working here, in a converted garage behind her parents' house, since she left school two years ago.

Unlike most violin makers, Ruth doesn't play the instrument particularly well. 'I tried for years,' she admits, 'but I was always more interested in how it worked than in the music.' At fourteen, she persuaded a local repairer to let her watch him work on Saturday mornings. He soon realised she had a gift. 'He started giving me small jobs, like replacing strings, and before long I was doing repairs he didn't have time for.'

Making a single violin takes Ruth around three months. Every stage is done by hand, from carving the back to cutting the delicate holes on the front. 'People sometimes ask why I don't use machines for the boring parts,' she says. 'The truth is, there are no boring parts. Each piece of wood is different, so you have to listen to it – literally. I tap it and listen to how it sounds, and that tells me how much more to take off.'

Selling her first violin was harder than making it. 'I'd put so much of myself into it that every price I thought of felt either too high or insultingly low,' she says. In the end, it was bought by a music student who had heard about Ruth through a friend. 'She sent me a recording of herself playing it a few weeks later. I cried, which was a bit embarrassing, but it was the moment I knew this was what I wanted to do.'

These days, Ruth has a waiting list of more than a year. Yet she has no plans to expand. 'I could take on an assistant and make twice as many violins,' she says, 'but then they wouldn't really be mine.' For now, she is happy in her garage, surrounded by wood and the occasional curious neighbour who pops in to see what all the tapping is about.

q.stem: What does Ruth's comment about her mother suggest?
opts: She is embarrassed by the state of the workshop.
She accepts that the workshop looks untidy.
She disagrees with her mother about most things.
She plans to move her workshop elsewhere.
q.hl: She's probably right, but I know exactly where everything is.
q.expl: Она соглашается, что мама, наверное, права (мастерская похожа на клетку хомяка), но её это не смущает: она знает, где что лежит.

q.stem: How did Ruth first become involved in making violins?
opts: She was taught by her violin teacher.
She spent time watching a professional at work.
She experimented with her own instrument.
q.hl: she persuaded a local repairer to let her watch him work
q.expl: В 14 лет она уговорила местного мастера разрешить ей смотреть, как он работает по субботам. Об учителе скрипки и школе речи нет.

q.stem: What does Ruth mean when she says 'you have to listen to it – literally'?
opts: She uses the sound of the wood to guide her work.
She likes to play music while she works.
She asks musicians for their opinion.
She prefers to work in complete silence.
q.hl: I tap it and listen to how it sounds, and that tells me how much more to take off.
q.expl: «Буквально» слушает: стучит по дереву и по звуку понимает, сколько ещё снять.

q.stem: Why did Ruth find it difficult to sell her first violin?
opts: She did not want to part with it.
She was unsure how much to ask for it.
Nobody seemed interested in buying it.
She thought it was not good enough.
q.hl: every price I thought of felt either too high or insultingly low
q.expl: Любая цена казалась то слишком высокой, то оскорбительно низкой, то есть она не знала, сколько просить. Ловушка A: она вложила в скрипку душу, но не говорит, что не хотела её продавать.

q.stem: Why was the recording the student sent important to Ruth?
opts: It showed her how to improve her work.
It helped her to find new customers.
It confirmed her choice of career.
It made her regret selling the violin.
q.hl: it was the moment I knew this was what I wanted to do
q.expl: Именно тогда она поняла, что хочет этим заниматься, — это подтверждение выбора профессии.

q.stem: What is Ruth's attitude to expanding her business?
opts: She would like to but cannot afford to.
She is waiting until she has more experience.
She prefers to keep making every instrument herself.
She is worried that demand will fall.
q.hl: but then they wouldn't really be mine
q.expl: С помощником скрипок стало бы вдвое больше, «но тогда они не были бы по-настоящему моими». Она хочет делать каждую сама.

parts.name: Gapped text
parts.instr: You are going to read an article about a woman who spent a year buying only second-hand things. Six sentences have been removed from the article. Choose from the sentences A–G the one which fits each gap (37–42). There is one extra sentence which you do not need to use.
parts.title: Twelve months, nothing new
parts.subtitle: Writer Clara Bell spent a year buying only second-hand. Here is what happened.
paras: It all started with a broken kettle. I was about to order a new one online when I realised I couldn't remember the last time I had repaired anything. [[37]] So I made a decision: for the next twelve months, I would buy nothing new except food and medicine.

The first few weeks were surprisingly easy. I found a kettle at a charity shop for three pounds, and a neighbour lent me a drill when a shelf fell down. [[38]] By the end of the second month, I was beginning to enjoy the challenge.

Things became harder when my laptop stopped working. I rely on it for work, and buying a second-hand one felt risky. [[39]] It took two weeks, but in the end I found a refurbished model that has worked perfectly ever since.
Clothes, on the other hand, were never a problem. [[40]] I discovered vintage markets I had walked past for years without noticing, and I swapped clothes with friends at regular 'swap parties'.

The hardest moment came at Christmas. Giving second-hand presents felt mean somehow, and I worried about what my family would think. [[41]] My nephew, who is eight, said the old wooden train set I'd found was the best present he had ever had.

Now that the year is over, I've gone back to buying some new things, but far fewer than before. [[42]] Last week, when my headphones broke, I didn't even think about replacing them – I just got out my tiny screwdriver.

sents.A: My parents' generation fixed things as a matter of course; mine simply replaced them.
sents.B: I even taught myself to sew a button back on, using a video online.
sents.C: I spent hours comparing websites and reading reviews before I trusted anyone.
sents.D: If anything, my wardrobe became more interesting than before.
sents.E: As it turned out, I needn't have worried.
sents.F: More importantly, I've lost the habit of seeing broken things as rubbish.
sents.G: My bank balance, I am pleased to say, has never looked healthier.

q.expl: Она не помнит, когда в последний раз что-то чинила, → обобщение: поколение родителей чинило, её поколение просто заменяет (A). Отсюда и решение «So I made a decision».
Продолжение списка мелких удач первых недель (чайник, дрель) — «I even taught myself to sew a button back on» (B).
Покупать б/у ноутбук рискованно → часами сравнивала сайты и читала отзывы (C) → «It took two weeks».
С одеждой проблем не было, «if anything» — даже наоборот, гардероб стал интереснее (D). Дальше — примеры: винтажные рынки и обмен одеждой.
Она волновалась, что подумает семья, → «As it turned out, I needn't have worried» (E) → племянник назвал подарок лучшим в жизни.
Теперь она не считает сломанные вещи мусором (F) — и пример: наушники сломались, а она взяла отвёртку. Ловушка G: про деньги логично, но не связано с примером про ремонт.

parts.name: Multiple matching
parts.instr: You are going to read an article in which four young people describe learning to drive. For questions 43–52, choose from the people (A–D). The people may be chosen more than once.
parts.title: Learning to drive

texts.name: Sam
texts.body: My dad offered to teach me himself to save money, which seemed like a great idea at the time. Within a fortnight we'd had so many arguments that my mum banned us from going out together. I switched to a professional instructor, and things improved straight away – she never raised her voice, no matter what I did. I failed my first test because I panicked at a busy roundabout, but I passed the second time a month later. Looking back, the failure probably did me good: I'm a much more careful driver because of it.

texts.name: Ella
texts.body: I learned in the middle of the city, which meant every lesson involved buses, cyclists and pedestrians stepping out without looking. I passed first time, which surprised everyone, including me. But to be honest, I hardly ever drive now. Parking is a nightmare and so expensive that it's simply not worth it, so I cycle almost everywhere. I'm still glad I've got my licence, though – it's useful to have for the future, especially if I ever move somewhere more rural.

texts.name: Josh
texts.body: Where I live, there's one bus a day, so a licence isn't a luxury – it's the only way to get to work. I couldn't wait months for lessons, so I did an intensive course: five days of driving, six hours a day, with the test at the end. It cost a lot more than ordinary lessons, and by the third day my brain felt like it was going to explode. But it worked, and I passed. I wouldn't recommend it to someone who gets stressed easily, though.

texts.name: Hana
texts.body: I was so nervous that I put off learning until I was twenty-one. In the end I needed over forty lessons before my instructor thought I was ready – most of my friends had needed about half that. He never once made me feel stupid, which made all the difference. When I finally passed, I cried in the car park. Now I drive my grandmother to the shops every Saturday, and she says I'm the best driver in the family. I'm not sure that's true, but it's nice to hear.

q.stem: had disagreements with a family member while learning?
q.hl: we'd had so many arguments that my mum banned us from going out together
q.expl: Сэм с папой так часто ссорились, что мама запретила им ездить вместе.

q.stem: believes that an early disappointment had a positive effect?
q.hl: the failure probably did me good
q.expl: Провал первого экзамена сделал Сэма более осторожным водителем.

q.stem: rarely uses their driving skills now?
q.expl: Элла почти не водит: парковка дорогая, она ездит на велосипеде.

q.stem: needed to learn quickly for practical reasons?
q.hl: I couldn't wait months for lessons
q.expl: Джошу права нужны, чтобы добираться до работы, ждать месяцами он не мог.

q.stem: needed more lessons than most people?
q.hl: most of my friends had needed about half that
q.expl: Хане понадобилось больше сорока уроков, друзьям — примерно вдвое меньше.

q.stem: was surprised by their own success?
q.hl: I passed first time, which surprised everyone, including me
q.expl: Элла сдала с первого раза и сама удивилась. Ловушка C: Джош тоже сдал, но удивления не выражает.

q.stem: warns that their way of learning is not suitable for everyone?
q.hl: I wouldn't recommend it to someone who gets stressed easily
q.expl: Интенсивный курс Джош не советует тем, кто легко нервничает.

q.stem: delayed starting to learn because of their feelings?
q.hl: I was so nervous that I put off learning until I was twenty-one
q.expl: Хана так нервничала, что откладывала до 21 года.

q.stem: noticed an immediate improvement after changing teachers?
q.expl: Сэм перешёл от папы к инструктору, и всё сразу наладилось. Ловушка D: у Ханы тоже хороший инструктор, но она его не меняла.

q.stem: has been praised by a relative for their driving?
q.hl: she says I'm the best driver in the family
q.expl: Бабушка говорит, что Хана — лучший водитель в семье.
